<h2>
  
  
  Vertical Slice Architecture in .NET — From N‑Tier Layers to Feature Slices
</h2>

<p>==========================================================================</p>

<p>Most .NET developers grow up on classic <strong>N‑Tier</strong> or <strong>Clean / Hexagonal</strong> architectures:</p>

<ul>
<li>Presentation layer</li>
<li>Application / Services layer</li>
<li>Domain</li>
<li>Data access</li>
</ul>

<p>Each layer is neatly stacked… but a <em>single feature</em> like <strong>"Get weather forecasts"</strong> ends up scattered across controllers, services, repositories, DTO folders, validators, and view‑models.</p>

<p>Vertical Slice Architecture (VSA) turns that on its head.</p>

<p>Instead of organizing code by <em>technical layer</em>, you organize it by <strong>feature</strong>. Each feature owns everything it needs — from the HTTP endpoint down to the data access — in one cohesive folder or <em>slice</em>.</p>

<p>In this post we’ll explore how to apply Vertical Slice Architecture in .NET using a minimal Web API, and we’ll refactor the classic <code>WeatherForecast</code> example into feature slices:</p>

<ul>
<li><code>GetForecasts</code></li>
<li><code>SearchForecasts</code></li>
</ul>

<p>Treat this as both a conceptual guide and a practical starter template you can drop into your next .NET Web API.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  Table of Contents
</h2>

<ol>
<li>What Is Vertical Slice Architecture?</li>

</ol>




<h2>
  
  
  1. What Is Vertical Slice Architecture?
</h2>

<p>Jimmy Bogard (creator of MediatR) describes Vertical Slice Architecture like this:</p>

<blockquote>
<p>“In this style, my architecture is built around distinct requests, encapsulating and grouping all concerns from front‑end to back. You take a normal ‘n‑tier’ or hexagonal/whatever architecture and remove the gates and barriers across those layers, and couple along the axis of change…”</p>
</blockquote>

<p>Put simply:</p>

<ul>
<li>A <strong>slice</strong> = a <strong>request / feature</strong> (e.g., <code>GetForecasts</code>, <code>CreateOrder</code>, <code>SearchCustomers</code>)</li>
<li>That slice owns everything required to fulfill that request:

<ul>
<li>HTTP endpoint (minimal API / controller)</li>
<li>Request &amp; response contracts</li>
<li>Handler / application logic</li>
<li>Domain rules needed for that feature</li>
<li>Data‑access logic (repository, Dapper query, EF Core query, search index call, etc.)</li>
</ul>


</li>

</ul>

<p>Instead of this:</p>

<ul>
<li>Controller folder</li>
<li>Services folder</li>
<li>Repositories folder</li>
<li>DTOs folder</li>
</ul>

<p>…you get this:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>Features/
  WeatherForecasts/
    GetForecasts/
    SearchForecasts/
  Orders/
    CreateOrder/
    CancelOrder/
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>Each subfolder is a slice that cuts <em>vertically</em> through the horizontal layers.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  2. From N‑Tier Layers to Slices (Mental Model)
</h2>

<p>Imagine a typical N‑Tier application as a cake with four horizontal layers:</p>

<ul>
<li>Presentation</li>
<li>Application</li>
<li>Domain</li>
<li>Data Access
</li>
</ul>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>+---------------------+  Presentation
+---------------------+  Application
+---------------------+  Domain
+---------------------+  Data Access
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>Now imagine you cut the cake into slices.</p>

<p>A <strong>Vertical Slice</strong> is one of those cuts: it touches <em>all</em> the layers, but only for a <strong>single feature</strong>.<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>    | Slice: GetForecasts |
+-------------------------+  Presentation
+-------------------------+  Application
+-------------------------+  Domain
+-------------------------+  Data Access
    | Slice: SearchForecasts |
</code></pre>

</div>



<p><em>Within</em> a slice we <strong>embrace</strong> coupling: the endpoint, request, handler, and data access all work together very closely.<br>
<em>Between</em> slices we aim for <strong>low coupling</strong>: features shouldn’t know about each other’s internal details.</p>

<p>Mental rule of thumb:</p>

<blockquote>
<p><strong>Maximize coupling <em>inside</em> a slice, minimize coupling <em>between</em> slices.</strong></p>
</blockquote>


<h2>
  
  
  3. Why Vertical Slice? Benefits &amp; Trade‑offs
</h2>

<p>Vertical Slice Architecture is about organizing code along the <strong>axis of change</strong> — features — instead of technical layers.</p>

<p><strong>Key benefits</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Feature isolation</strong><br><br>
You build and modify one slice without worrying about breaking another. Each feature is “master of its own destiny”.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Parallel development</strong><br><br>
Teams can work on different slices without constantly touching shared service/repository layers.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>New features only add code</strong><br><br>
Done right, you almost never have to edit some giant <code>Services</code> or <code>Infrastructure</code> class. New feature? → new slice.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Screaming architecture</strong><br><br>
Open the <code>Features</code> folder and the <em>use cases</em> of the system literally “scream” at you (<code>CreateInvoice</code>, <code>RefundPayment</code>, <code>SearchForecasts</code>, …).</p></li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Trade‑offs / costs</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Possible duplication</strong><br><br>
Without discipline, utility helpers, validation rules, or mapping code might be duplicated across slices.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Learning curve</strong><br><br>
Teams used to layered architectures may initially find slices “weird” or “too coupled”.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Harder to over‑standardize</strong><br><br>
Because each slice can choose how it talks to persistence or other services, standardization requires good guidelines and code reviews.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>As with any architecture choice, you’re managing trade‑offs to deliver business value faster and safer.</p>


<h2>
  
  
  4. Starting Point: The Default .NET Web API
</h2>

<p>We’ll start from the default <code>dotnet new webapi</code> / minimal API template with the classic <code>WeatherForecast</code> example.</p>

<p>Initially the project looks roughly like this:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>Vertical.Slice.WebApi/
  Properties/
  appsettings.json
  Program.cs
  WeatherForecast.cs
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>The single <code>Program.cs</code> file usually contains the endpoint:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight csharp"><code><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">MapGet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"/weatherforecast"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">summaries</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="k">new</span><span class="p">[]</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="s">"Freezing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Bracing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Chilly"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Cool"</span> <span class="p">};</span>
    <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">forecast</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="n">Enumerable</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="m">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">5</span><span class="p">).</span><span class="nf">Select</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span>
        <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">WeatherForecast</span><span class="p">(</span>
            <span class="n">DateOnly</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">FromDateTime</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DateTime</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Now</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">AddDays</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">)),</span>
            <span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(-</span><span class="m">20</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">55</span><span class="p">),</span>
            <span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Length</span><span class="p">)]))</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">ToArray</span><span class="p">();</span>

    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">forecast</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">});</span>
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>Our goal is to <strong>pull this endpoint out</strong> into a proper <strong>slice</strong> and then add another slice for searching forecasts.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  5. Step 1 — Create a Features Folder
</h2>

<p>First, create a screaming architecture root folder:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>Vertical.Slice.WebApi/
  Features/
    WeatherForecasts/
      GetForecasts/
      SearchForecasts/
  Program.cs
  appsettings.json
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>Start with one slice:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>Features/
  WeatherForecasts/
    GetForecasts/
      GetForecasts.cs
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>We’ll keep everything for the <code>GetForecasts</code> request inside this file: request, response, handler, and endpoint.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  6. Step 2 — Implement the GetForecasts Slice
</h2>

<p>Inside <code>Features/WeatherForecasts/GetForecasts/GetForecasts.cs</code> we can define the full slice:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight csharp"><code><span class="k">namespace</span> <span class="nn">Vertical.Slice.WebApi.Features.WeatherForecasts.GetForecasts</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">GetForecastsEndpoint</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="n">Route</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="s">"/weatherforecast"</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="k">void</span> <span class="nf">MapGetForecasts</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">this</span> <span class="n">IEndpointRouteBuilder</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">MapGet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Route</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">Handle</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">WithName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"GetForecasts"</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">WithSummary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Gets the next 5 weather forecasts"</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Produces</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="n">GetForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">&gt;();</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="n">IResult</span> <span class="nf">Handle</span><span class="p">()</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">summaries</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="k">new</span><span class="p">[]</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="s">"Freezing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Bracing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Chilly"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Cool"</span> <span class="p">};</span>

        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">forecasts</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="n">Enumerable</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="m">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">5</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Select</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">(</span>
                <span class="n">DateOnly</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">FromDateTime</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DateTime</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Now</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">AddDays</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">)),</span>
                <span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(-</span><span class="m">20</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">55</span><span class="p">),</span>
                <span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Length</span><span class="p">)]</span>
            <span class="p">))</span>
            <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">ToArray</span><span class="p">();</span>

        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">response</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">GetForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">forecasts</span><span class="p">);</span>

        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">Results</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Ok</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">response</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">record</span> <span class="nc">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DateOnly</span> <span class="n">Date</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">TemperatureC</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="n">Summary</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">TemperatureF</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="m">32</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="p">)(</span><span class="n">TemperatureC</span> <span class="p">/</span> <span class="m">0.5556</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">record</span> <span class="nc">GetForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IReadOnlyList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="n">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="n">Items</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre>

</div>



<p><strong>What lives in this slice?</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Endpoint</strong> (<code>MapGetForecasts</code>, <code>Handle</code>)</li>
<li>
<strong>DTOs</strong> (<code>ForecastDto</code>, <code>GetForecastsResponse</code>)</li>
<li>No extra service/repository types — just enough to fetch and shape the data for this feature.</li>
</ul>

<p>Later, if you introduce a database or a search index, you can refactor <em>inside</em> this slice without leaking those details to others.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  7. Step 3 — Implement the SearchForecasts Slice
</h2>

<p>Now we’ll add a second slice that lets clients search by minimum temperature.</p>

<p>Folder structure:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code>Features/
  WeatherForecasts/
    GetForecasts/
      GetForecasts.cs
    SearchForecasts/
      SearchForecasts.cs
</code></pre>

</div>



<p><code>SearchForecasts.cs</code>:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight csharp"><code><span class="k">namespace</span> <span class="nn">Vertical.Slice.WebApi.Features.WeatherForecasts.SearchForecasts</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">SearchForecastsEndpoint</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="n">Route</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="s">"/weatherforecast/search"</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="k">void</span> <span class="nf">MapSearchForecasts</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">this</span> <span class="n">IEndpointRouteBuilder</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">MapGet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Route</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">Handle</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">WithName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"SearchForecasts"</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">WithSummary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Searches forecasts with a minimum temperature filter"</span><span class="p">)</span>
           <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Produces</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="n">SearchForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">&gt;();</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">static</span> <span class="n">IResult</span> <span class="nf">Handle</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">AsParameters</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="n">SearchForecastsRequest</span> <span class="n">request</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">summaries</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="k">new</span><span class="p">[]</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="s">"Freezing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Bracing"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Chilly"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Cool"</span> <span class="p">};</span>

        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">forecasts</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="n">Enumerable</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="m">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">20</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Select</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">(</span>
                <span class="n">DateOnly</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">FromDateTime</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DateTime</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Now</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">AddDays</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">)),</span>
                <span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(-</span><span class="m">20</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="m">55</span><span class="p">),</span>
                <span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Shared</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Next</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">summaries</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">Length</span><span class="p">)]</span>
            <span class="p">))</span>
            <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Where</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="n">f</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">TemperatureC</span> <span class="p">&gt;=</span> <span class="n">request</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">MinTemperatureC</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">ToArray</span><span class="p">();</span>

        <span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">response</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">SearchForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">forecasts</span><span class="p">);</span>

        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">Results</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Ok</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">response</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">record</span> <span class="nc">SearchForecastsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">MinTemperatureC</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="p">-</span><span class="m">10</span><span class="p">);</span>

<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">record</span> <span class="nc">SearchForecastsResponse</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IReadOnlyList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="n">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="n">Items</span><span class="p">);</span>

<span class="c1">// We can reuse ForecastDto from the GetForecasts slice,</span>
<span class="c1">// or define a local version if we want full isolation.</span>
<span class="k">public</span> <span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">record</span> <span class="nc">ForecastDto</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DateOnly</span> <span class="n">Date</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">TemperatureC</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="n">Summary</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">public</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">TemperatureF</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="m">32</span> <span class="p">+</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="p">)(</span><span class="n">TemperatureC</span> <span class="p">/</span> <span class="m">0.5556</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>Notice a few things:</p>

<ul>
<li>The request is explicitly modeled as <code>SearchForecastsRequest</code>.</li>
<li>The slice is free to <strong>shape data differently</strong> than <code>GetForecasts</code> if needed.</li>
<li>Internally, this slice might later query <strong>a completely different data store</strong> (e.g., ElasticSearch, Azure Cognitive Search) without affecting <code>GetForecasts</code> at all.</li>
</ul>

<p>That’s the power of slices: each feature decides <em>how</em> it gets its work done.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  8. Wiring Slices into Program.cs
</h2>

<p>Finally, <code>Program.cs</code> turns into a thin composition root:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight csharp"><code><span class="k">using</span> <span class="nn">Vertical.Slice.WebApi.Features.WeatherForecasts.GetForecasts</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="nn">Vertical.Slice.WebApi.Features.WeatherForecasts.SearchForecasts</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">builder</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="n">WebApplication</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">CreateBuilder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">args</span><span class="p">);</span>

<span class="c1">// Add services here (DbContext, logging, etc.)</span>

<span class="kt">var</span> <span class="n">app</span> <span class="p">=</span> <span class="n">builder</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Build</span><span class="p">();</span>

<span class="c1">// Map feature slices</span>
<span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">MapGetForecasts</span><span class="p">();</span>
<span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">MapSearchForecasts</span><span class="p">();</span>

<span class="n">app</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">Run</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>The app startup doesn’t know about controllers, services, or repositories. It only knows it’s mapping <strong>feature endpoints</strong>.</p>

<p>As you add more slices (<code>CreateForecast</code>, <code>DeleteForecast</code>, etc.), you simply call their mapping extension methods here.</p>




<h2>
  
  
  9. Pros, Cons, and When to Use VSA
</h2>

<h3>
  
  
  Pros
</h3>

<p><strong>1. Creation of slices in isolation</strong><br><br>
Each feature can be designed, implemented, and tested in its own folder, with its own dependencies. This scales very well for larger teams: multiple developers can work on different features without trampling on each other’s shared service layers.</p>

<p><strong>2. Safe modification of logic within a slice</strong><br><br>
Because a slice doesn’t leak its internals, changes are localized. You can swap a SQL query for a search index call without breaking other features.</p>

<p><strong>3. New code mostly adds new files</strong><br><br>
Mature VSA projects trend towards “append‑only” feature development: new requirements → new slices, not edits to a global application service that every endpoint uses.</p>

<h3>
  
  
  Cons / considerations
</h3>

<p><strong>1. Potential duplication across slices</strong><br><br>
Without careful refactoring, shared logic (e.g., common validation, mapping, error handling) might be copied into multiple slices. Periodic extraction of true cross‑cutting concerns into shared libraries is important.</p>

<p><strong>2. Architecture learning curve</strong><br><br>
Teams raised on strictly layered architectures might initially feel uncomfortable with a handler talking directly to a DbContext or Dapper query that lives inside the same folder as the endpoint.</p>

<p><strong>3. Harder to over‑standardize</strong><br><br>
Because each slice solves a specific problem, it can be tempting to let every slice “do its own thing”. Lightweight standards (e.g., “each slice defines Request, Handler, Response, Endpoint”) and good reviews help preserve consistency without killing flexibility.</p>

<h3>
  
  
  When Vertical Slice shines
</h3>

<ul>
<li>Product or SaaS codebases with many evolving features</li>
<li>API‑first systems with lots of request/response endpoints</li>
<li>Teams that want to parallelize development by feature</li>
<li>Codebases adopting CQRS + MediatR (each handler naturally maps to a slice)</li>
</ul>




<h2>
  
  
  10. Next Steps: MediatR, CQRS, and Beyond
</h2>

<p>Once you’re comfortable with the basic folder structure, you can <strong>layer more patterns on top</strong> of VSA:</p>

<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>MediatR / CQRS</strong> — Model each request as a command or query (<code>IRequest&lt;TResponse&gt;</code>) and let MediatR dispatch to handlers. Your slice then holds:</p>

<ul>
<li><code>GetForecastsQuery</code></li>
<li><code>GetForecastsQueryHandler</code></li>
<li><code>GetForecastsEndpoint</code></li>
<li><code>GetForecastsResponse</code></li>
</ul>


</li>

<li><p><strong>Validation</strong> — Use FluentValidation or custom validators per slice. Each feature owns its input validation and error shaping.</p></li>

<li>

<p><strong>Persistence</strong> — Inside the slice, you’re free to:</p>

<ul>
<li>Use EF Core DbContext</li>
<li>Call stored procedures</li>
<li>Hit a read‑optimized search store</li>
<li>Call external services</li>
</ul>


</li>

<li><p><strong>Testing</strong> — Because slices are self‑contained, you can write focused unit and integration tests that exercise the feature end‑to‑end.</p></li>

</ul>




<h2>
  
  
  Conclusion
</h2>

<p>Vertical Slice Architecture is not a silver bullet, but it’s a powerful way to align your .NET code with how your product actually changes: <strong>one feature at a time</strong>.</p>

<p>By organizing around slices instead of layers you get:</p>

<ul>
<li>Architecture that “screams” your use cases</li>
<li>Safer, more isolated changes</li>
<li>Better parallelization for teams</li>
<li>Flexibility to choose the right persistence or integration strategy per feature</li>
</ul>

<p>Start small:</p>

<ol>
<li>Take an existing Web API feature.</li>
<li>Move its endpoint, request, response, and handler into a single folder.</li>
<li>Repeat for the next feature.</li>
</ol>

<p>Before long, you’ll find your codebase reads more like a product specification than a wiring diagram of controllers and services.</p>

<p>Happy slicing, and happy coding in .NET! 🍰</p>
